applicant_utility.summary: Two documents decide this award: your Manchester offer and the online form that arrives by email only after that offer, so the sequence matters - apply for the course first, then wait for the form rather than hunting for an application portal. Check the South Asia rule carefully: your bachelor's degree must have been taken within South Asia, which quietly excludes applicants who studied their first degree in the UK or elsewhere. The £12,000 is a first-year tuition discount on multi-year courses, so on a two-year master's it covers roughly a fraction of your total fee bill and none of your living costs - budget accordingly.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Self-funded students domiciled in Bangladesh, Pakistan or Sri Lanka who took their bachelor's degree in South Asia and hold an offer for an eligible on-campus Manchester master's.

applicant_utility.summary: Timing here is offer-driven: the International Office emails the scholarship application form only to relevant offer-holders, so your practical deadline is the course offer date, not the scholarship calendar. There is exactly one scholarship for Bangladesh, so odds are long even among well-qualified offer-holders - keep a parallel funding plan. Note the stacking rule: if you are offered both this and a Global Futures Scholarship you must pick one, and you cannot hold another internal full tuition award alongside it, so model the total package before accepting.
